method: Five frames sampled at 1s/5s/9s/13s/17s, downscaled to 200px wide, 113,000 pixels analysed. Darkest and lightest deciles averaged; accent isolated as green-dominant saturated pixels.
why_this_exists: CHEAP_PRODUCTION_ECONOMICS_V1 says the premium anchor is the style REFERENCE the cheap tiers are graded against. That was documented and not executed: the plates on disk were generated independently of the anchor. These are the anchor's actual values, so cheap tiers can be graded to it IN THE PROMPT rather than colour-corrected afterwards.
findings: THE ANCHOR IS A LIGHT FRAME. Mean luminance 161.9 of 255. Grading plates to a near-black ground would NOT match it - they would read as a different piece cut in beside it.

THE BRAND ACCENT DOES NOT APPEAR AS SPECIFIED. BRAND.md's #7cfc00 renders as #7fb449 in this take's lighting: darker, less saturated, olive rather than chartreuse. Grade cheap tiers to the APPEARANCE (#7fb449), not to the spec (#7cfc00), or they clash with the very asset they are meant to match.
THE ACCENT IS 1.31% OF FRAME AREA. It is trim on the presenter's jacket, not a field of colour. A plate flooded with lime would overpower the anchor rather than match it.
The 'paper' palette already chosen for this drop is therefore correct - but it was correct by argument, before anyone measured the take.
measurement_discipline_note: ffmpeg palettegen initially reported #00ff00 at full saturation as a dominant colour. That is palettegen's transparency sentinel, not a colour present in the take - every other entry in that palette was muted mauve and cream. Recording it would have graded every cheap asset to a colour that does not exist. Real frames were sampled instead.

grading_directives_for_cheap_tiers.ground: Light, warm-neutral. Target mean luminance 150-175, not a dark ground.
grading_directives_for_cheap_tiers.accent_usage: A single small accent incident occupying roughly 1-2% of frame. Never a lime field, never a lime gradient.
grading_directives_for_cheap_tiers.accent_value: #7fb449 as rendered. Reserve #7cfc00 for vector and type, where the value is literal and unlit.
grading_directives_for_cheap_tiers.prompt_fragment: warm neutral daylight interior, soft diffuse light, near-white walls, muted mauve-grey shadows, one small olive-green accent object occupying a tiny fraction of frame, 50mm, eye-level, shallow depth of field, real material wear, no text of any kind, deliberate empty area for typography

boundaries: Measured from ONE take. A second take under different lighting will move these values; re-measure rather than assuming.
This describes how the anchor LOOKS. It is not a brand specification and does not override BRAND.md or Design DNA v1 for surfaces not being matched to this take.
